subject.title: EPERM crashes on database files during active locks in applyPrivateModeSync

question: How should shared-state SQLite permission hardening handle EPERM on live WAL/SHM sidecars when the parent state directory is private but the sidecar mode is still broad?
rationale: The availability failure is source-plausible, but the same helper controls credentials-adjacent permission hardening and current tests intentionally keep ordinary broad-mode EPERM fatal.

options.title: Scope tolerance to live sidecars
options.body: Tolerate or defer EPERM only for SQLite sidecars under a private state directory, log degraded hardening, and keep directory/main-file ownership failures fatal.

options.title: Require live proof first
options.body: Ask for a concrete active-lock reproduction or platform log before changing the fail-closed EPERM policy.

options.title: Keep fail-closed unchanged
options.body: Treat unresolved EPERM on broad-mode database files as a security boundary and leave recovery to explicit operator repair.

recommendation.title: Scope tolerance to live sidecars
recommendation.body: Tolerate or defer EPERM only for SQLite sidecars under a private state directory, log degraded hardening, and keep directory/main-file ownership failures fatal.
